newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST-Singapore Feb exports to grow modestly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Singapore Feb exports to grow modestly.

text.p: Singapore's February non-oil export figures are likely to signal a tentative recovery as the electronics industry remains sluggish, a Reuters poll of economists said on Tuesday.
A survey of 16 financial institutions this week showed an average forecast of 1.5 percent rise year-on-year in nominal terms for non-oil exports in February.

Forecasts, however, were unusually disparate, ranging from minus 5.0 percent to plus 10 percent -- a reflection of general uncertainty about the uptrend in exports after a weaker-than-expected January manufacturing growth, they said.
Economists blamed the 7.2 percent drop in January industrial output for perceptions of continued weakness in exports.
Export orders were seen on the mend, with the worst period behind the market, but the upward momentum could be slowed by the slide in electronics output early this year.
Singapore's non-oil domestic exports for January registered a 3.1 percent decline year-on-year, and electronics production actually saw a hefty fall of 10.9 percent.
Some economists predicted a slight rise for February year-on-year on the basis there were fewer days in the month and firmer exports this year would be higher in percentage terms.
Some also gave projections on a seasonally-adjusted basis, accounting for Chinese New Year and Moslem Eid festival holidays.
The consensus was that February, sandwiched between Christmas and these other festivals, was historically more volatile and prone to wider swings in forecasts than usual.
Overall, external trade was seen still making slow headway with scant evidence yet of a convincing economic turnaround.
While U.S. semi-conductor orders started firming in the fourth quarter of 1996, much of this would not trickle down to Asian manufacturers until April-May at the earliest, economists said.
